problem_statement: Two blocks of masses $m_1 = 3.0\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 1.0\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a uniform solid cylindrical pulley of mass $M = 2.0\text{ kg}$ and radius $R = 0.10\text{ m}$. The pulley rotates about a frictionless horizontal axle through its center, and the string does not slip on the pulley rim. Taking $g = 9.80\text{ m/s}^2$, find: (a) the linear acceleration $a$ of the blocks, and (b) the string tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ on each side of the pulley.
target_quantity: Linear acceleration a and tensions T_1, T_2
governing_principles: Newton's Second Law for translating blocks: sum F = m a
Rotational dynamic equation for massive pulley: tau_net = (T_1 - T_2) R = I alpha
Moment of inertia of solid cylindrical pulley: I = 1/2 M R^2
No-slip kinematic constraint: a = R alpha
solution_strategy: 1. Draw free body diagrams for m_1, m_2, and the pulley. 2. Write linear equations: m_1 g - T_1 = m_1 a, and T_2 - m_2 g = m_2 a. 3. Write torque equation: (T_1 - T_2) R = 1/2 M R^2 (a / R) => T_1 - T_2 = 1/2 M a. 4. Sum all three equations to eliminate internal tensions and solve for acceleration a. 5. Substitute a back to obtain T_1 and T_2.

ordered_steps.principle_applied: Newton's Second Law for descending block m_1
Newton's Second Law for ascending block m_2
Rotational dynamic relation for pulley with no-slip constraint
ordered_steps.equation: \tau_{\text{net}} = (T_1 - T_2) R = I \alpha = \left( \frac{1}{2} M R^2 \right) \left( \frac{a}{R} \right) \implies T_1 - T_2 = \frac{1}{2} M a

ordered_steps.principle_applied: System summation to solve for linear acceleration
ordered_steps.equation: (m_1 - m_2) g = \left( m_1 + m_2 + \frac{1}{2} M \right) a \implies a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2) g}{m_1 + m_2 + \frac{1}{2} M}
T_1 = m_1 (g - a), \quad T_2 = m_2 (g + a)

sanity_checks: Tension difference check: T_1 - T_2 = 17.64 - 13.72 = 3.92 N. Pulley inertial term: 1/2 M a = 1/2(2.0)(3.92) = 3.92 N. Exact match!
Massless pulley limit: M -> 0 yields a = 2(9.8)/4 = 4.90 m/s^2, higher acceleration as expected.
Tension hierarchy: m_1 g = 29.4 N > T_1 = 17.64 N > T_2 = 13.72 N > m_2 g = 9.8 N, completely consistent with downward acceleration of m_1 and upward acceleration of m_2.
alternate_methods: Work-Energy theorem: Delta K = Delta U => 1/2 (m_1 + m_2 + 1/2 M) v^2 = (m_1 - m_2) g y. Differentiating with respect to time yields identical a.
